digits.description: Fires on numerical tokens (e.g., <<1>>(10)) in contexts involving dates, statistics, or historical events, especially when followed by years, percentages, or time spans. Common in factual or historical narratives.

the.description: Fires strongly on the definite article 'the' (case-insensitive) when it introduces a specific noun or concept, often in formal or explanatory contexts. Common in academic, technical, or descriptive writing where clarity and specificity are emphasized.

comma.description: Fires strongly on commas (<<,>>(10)) in informational or explanatory contexts, often separating clauses in technical, educational, or descriptive texts. Common in lists, definitions, and cause-effect structures. Appears in academic, governmental, and instructional writing.

capitalised word.description: Fires strongly on specific proper nouns (e.g., 'Government', 'England', 'Channel') and definite articles ('The', 'This') in contexts involving locations, organizations, or technical terms. Often precedes additional descriptors or specific names.

of.description: Fires strongly on the preposition 'of' when it follows a noun or concept and introduces a specification, explanation, or example, such as in phrases like 'degree of transformation', 'summer of 2009', or 'source of radiation'.

full stop.description: Fires strongly on periods <<.>>(10) following full sentences, especially at the end of statements in formal or explanatory contexts, often in academic, historical, or technical writing.

and.description: Fires strongly on 'and' connecting two nouns, phrases, or clauses, especially in lists, compound subjects, or explanatory contexts. Common in factual, descriptive, or procedural text where items or ideas are combined logically or sequentially.

is/are/was/were.description: This neuron fires strongly (10) on the verbs 'is' and 'are' when they follow a noun or noun phrase, typically in declarative sentences that state definitions, facts, or characteristics. It appears in general informational or explanatory contexts, often in academic, technical, or descriptive writing. The structure is usually [Subject] <<is/are>>(10) [description/definition].

in.description: Fires strongly on 'in' when indicating location, time, or medium (e.g., 'in the year', 'in Jerusalem', 'in water'), often followed by a noun or place. Common in descriptive or historical contexts.

pronoun.description: This neuron fires strongly (10) on personal pronouns like 'it', 'they', 'she', and 'he' when referring back to a previously mentioned subject in a general explanatory or descriptive context. It typically follows a noun or concept and is used to continue elaborating on that subject, often introducing a new aspect or consequence.
